subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw initially accept only canonical core readiness conditions and legacy-compatible projections, or commit now to the full provider, hosting-profile, CLI, artifact-identity, and release-conformance contract?
rationale: Implementation proof establishes feasibility but cannot determine which permanent availability, configuration, plugin API, CLI, and support promises maintainers intend to own.

options.title: Accept a staged foundation
options.body: Approve core conditions and compatibility projections first, then require separate acceptance for broader provider, profile, CLI, and release surfaces.

options.title: Accept the full contract
options.body: Approve all proposed surfaces and explicitly own their compatibility and packaged release-test obligations.

options.title: Keep hosting composition external
options.body: Retain fixed Gateway readiness and leave supplemental hosting checks to hosts or plugins.

recommendation.title: Accept a staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve core conditions and compatibility projections first, then require separate acceptance for broader provider, profile, CLI, and release surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history directly connects this person to the RFC template, acceptance lifecycle, and a recently accepted RFC, while runtime owners can advise on technical details.
